P5 is the main loss channel, at roughly $5.5M from the spread and about $0.2M from the higher load. P2 offsets about $0.7M, and P1 and P4 lose about $0.5M together. The net loss is roughly $5.3M. The short, concentrated window tests how the book responds to a sharp pocket event rather than a sustained one.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Henry Hub falls 40% over 20 days because of a supply glut and mild demand. The lower gas price pulls WEST on-peak down through the gas-linked marginal cost, which hurts P1 and slightly hurts P4 because the heat-rate call moves toward zero. Real-time prices clear 30% above day-ahead, which costs P3 on its off-peak receive position. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $70/MWh because pocket transmission stays constrained while upstate supply weakens. Load runs 10% above normal over the 20 days, which adds to the retail obligation. P5 carries roughly $5.2M from the spread and about $0.5M from load. P2 offsets about $0.8M. P1, P3 and P4 together lose about $0.7M. The net loss is roughly $5.5M. This scenario differs from the others in combining a gas-price decline with a real-time premium, so the book's sensitivity to the sign of the gas move and the dart move is tested together.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Slower-than-forecast arrival of large new loads cuts the summer daily peak by about 1,500 MW (load_peak_ratio 0.95 against a 31,600 MW normal summer peak), and day-ahead commitments overshoot real-time demand for 30 days. Real-time clears 70% below day-ahead (dart_pct -70), which lowers WEST on-peak prices by a further 70% (ref_onpeak_pct -70) on top of the load and gas moves. Henry Hub falls 50% (gas_hh_pct -50) in a soft summer market. P1 (long WEST swap) and P4 (heat-rate call, WEST-linked) lose value, and P3 is largely unaffected. The loss is an engine-linear estimate of about $5.46M, not a verified result.

analogue.dates: 2025 Gold Book edition (dates not given in table)

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: A moderate large-load shortfall of about 900 MW (load_peak_ratio 0.97, large_load_shock_mw -900) reduces summer peak load, but the main loss channel is congestion. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $70/MWh for 30 days (pocket_minus_ref_usd +70), which is inside the summer implausible ceiling of 363.1 and below the historical maximum of 289.7 for this factor. This requires a concurrent Zone J import or transmission derate that the load shortfall does not itself imply, so the physical coherence is weak. Small WEST declines (ref_onpeak_pct -5) and the load reduction add minor losses. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.75M, which is unverified.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Slower large-load arrivals of about 1,400 MW (large_load_shock_mw -1400, load_peak_ratio 0.96) coincide with a concentrated 10-day Zone J congestion event. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $200/MWh for 10 days (pocket_minus_ref_usd +200), which is above the historical summer maximum of 289.7 but below the implausible ceiling of 363.1. The mechanism is a Zone J import limit or peaker-retention constraint that keeps N.Y.C. prices high while WEST softens modestly (ref_onpeak_pct -20). Real-time and gas are held flat in this case, so the loss comes almost entirely from the short P5 retail exposure. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.47M, which is unverified.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Large new loads arrive about 1,500 MW slower than forecast, cutting the summer daily peak to 0.95 of normal (large_load_shock_mw -1500, load_peak_ratio 0.95). Oversupply of committed capacity pushes WEST on-peak prices down 88% on top of the load effect (ref_onpeak_pct -88), which is inside the summer implausible-below ceiling of -90.8. Henry Hub falls 40% (gas_hh_pct -40), lowering the heat-rate call P4 and the WEST long swap P1 together. N.Y.C. minus WEST widens by $40/MWh (pocket_minus_ref_usd +40), a moderate Zone J congestion effect that hurts the short retail position P5 while P2 partly offsets. Day-ahead and real-time are held at parity (dart_pct 0). The loss is dominated by P1 and P4. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.6M, which is unverified.

analogue.dates: 2025 Gold Book edition (dates not given in table)

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: A 1,000 MW large-load shortfall (large_load_shock_mw -1000, load_peak_ratio 0.97) lowers summer load modestly, while a Zone J transmission limit or retained-peaker constraint widens N.Y.C. minus WEST by $150/MWh (pocket_minus_ref_usd +150) for 15 days. This is within the summer historical maximum and implausible ceiling range for the factor but requires a concurrent import constraint that the load shortfall does not itself imply, so coherence is weak. WEST on-peak falls 60% (ref_onpeak_pct -60) as surplus upstate supply is curtailed by low-value demand. Gas falls 30% (gas_hh_pct -30). The retail short P5 and the congestion-linked P2 dominate the outcome. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.3M, which is unverified.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: A five-day burst of slower large-load arrivals (large_load_shock_mw -900, load_peak_ratio 0.97) combines a sharp WEST on-peak collapse (ref_onpeak_pct -88) with a $150/MWh widening of N.Y.C. minus WEST (pocket_minus_ref_usd +150). Gas falls 30% (gas_hh_pct -30), reducing P4 and P1 value. The short-duration design concentrates the WEST move on the long swap P1 and the heat-rate call P4, while the congestion widening hits P5, with P2 offsetting part of that loss. Dart is neutral, so real-time spike risk is not used. This keeps the scenario distinct from the 30-day system case and from the Zone J congestion case. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.5M, which is unverified and based on the five-day sensitivity table.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Large new loads arrive about 700 MW slower than forecast, trimming the summer daily peak to 0.98 of normal (large_load_shock_mw -700, load_peak_ratio 0.98). Real-time clears 15% above day-ahead (dart_pct +15) as the day-ahead commitment undershoots the realised evening peak, which hurts the day-ahead-short-real-time-long P3 position. A Zone J transmission or retained-peaker constraint widens N.Y.C. minus WEST by $100/MWh for 20 days (pocket_minus_ref_usd +100), which is inside the summer historical maximum of 289.7 for this factor. WEST on-peak falls 15% (ref_onpeak_pct -15) and Henry Hub falls 20% (gas_hh_pct -20), lowering P1 and P4. The main loss is the short retail obligation P5, partly offset by the congestion-long P2. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.4M, which is unverified and assumes the Zone J constraint is not already priced in.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: Large-load arrivals run about 1,500 MW slower than forecast (large_load_shock_mw -1500), and the summer daily peak falls to 0.95 of normal (load_peak_ratio 0.95). Upstate oversupply collapses WEST on-peak prices by 90% (ref_onpeak_pct -90), close to the summer implausible-below ceiling of -90.8. Henry Hub falls 50% (gas_hh_pct -50), reducing the heat-rate call P4 on top of the long WEST swap P1. N.Y.C. minus WEST widens only modestly, by $25/MWh (pocket_minus_ref_usd +25), so the retail short P5 contributes a smaller share than in the congestion cases. Day-ahead and real-time remain at parity (dart_pct 0). The loss is driven mainly by P1 and P4, with P5 a secondary contributor. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.6M, which is unverified.

label: LIVE CLAUDE | REAL DATA - NYISO (reference WEST, pocket N.Y.C.), fit window 2019-01-01 to 2025-12-31, panel 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-30
narrative: A 10-day burst of slower large-load arrivals (large_load_shock_mw -1400, load_peak_ratio 0.96) combines a real-time premium with a sharp Zone J congestion widening. Real-time clears 120% above day-ahead (dart_pct +120), which is inside the summer implausible-above ceiling of 284.7 but above the historical maximum of 207.8, so it is treated as a stressed case. N.Y.C. minus WEST widens by $180/MWh (pocket_minus_ref_usd +180) for the same 10 days, below the implausible ceiling of 363.1. WEST on-peak falls 20% (ref_onpeak_pct -20) and gas is held flat, so the loss comes mainly from the short retail P5 and the real-time exposure of P3. P2 offsets part of the loss. The engine-linear estimate is about $5.2M, which is unverified and requires the real-time spike and congestion widening to co-occur.
